Property Address: Extract all complete property addresses mentioned in the lease document, including building names/numbers as standalone strings. Include street, city, state, and zip code if available. DO NOT include notice addresses, mailing addresses for rent payment, or any surrounding commentary like 'The property is located at...' or 'Premises known as...'. Only extract the physical property location addresses.
Premises: Extract the description of the leased premises from this lease. Include the rentable square footage, floor number or level, and any specific description of the space being leased. Look for sections titled 'Premises', 'Leased Premises', or 'Description of Premises'.
Landlord: Extract the exact full legal name of the Landlord as it appears in the lease. If the Landlord is described as a 'Delaware limited liability company' or similar entity type, include this designation as part of the name. DO NOT return any explanatory notes, headings, or labels like 'Landlord:'. Only return the exact entity name and type, for example: 'XYZ Corporation, a Delaware limited liability company'.
Tenant: Extract the exact full legal name of the Tenant as it appears in the lease. If the Tenant name includes a designation like 'a California corporation', include that phrase in the extracted output. DO NOT add entity designations if they are not explicitly mentioned. DO NOT return explanatory notes or labels. Only extract the Tenant's name, not the Landlord or any other parties.
Guarantor: Extract only the name(s) of the Guarantor(s) as explicitly stated in the lease. Look specifically for sections or clauses containing the keyword 'Guarantor' or 'Guarantors'. Return the exact full legal name(s) as written. If multiple guarantors are listed, include all names separated by commas.
Other Surety: Extract information about any other forms of security or surety mentioned in the lease beyond guarantors and security deposits. This may include letters of credit, performance bonds, parent company guarantees, or other financial assurances.
Permitted Uses: Please provide a formal and concise legal abstract for all the information about the permitted uses of the premises as stated in the lease. It could include the summary of all allowed activities, business types, or purposes for which the tenant may use the space. List them clearly and concisely as they appear in the lease document.
Term: Please provide a formal legal abstract for all the information about the lease term. If available, please include the following details in the abstract (totally skip from response if something is not found): (1) The total duration of the initial lease term in months or years, (2) start date (Term Commencement Date), (3) end date (Term Expiration Date) (4) any extension options if mentioned. Please highlight any dates or any clearly specified time period in concise format.
Lease Commencement Date: Extract the exact date when the lease term begins (Term Commencement Date). This is typically stated as a specific calendar date or defined as a date calculated from certain conditions. Include the exact wording if it's conditional (e.g., 'the later of [date] or [event]'). DO NOT confuse this with the execution date or rent commencement date.
Rent Commencement Date: Extract the exact date when the tenant's obligation to pay rent begins (Rent Commencement Date). This may differ from the Lease Commencement Date. If there is a free rent period or rent abatement, indicate when rent payments actually start. Include exact wording if it's conditional.
Expiration Date: Extract the exact date when the initial lease term ends. CRITICAL CALCULATION: When lease says 'the date that is X months after [start date]', add exactly X months to the start date. EXAMPLE: 'Term Expiration Date: 120 months after February 1, 2025' = February 1, 2035 (NOT November 30, 2034). 120 months = 10 years exactly, same day of month. If a specific calendar date is stated (e.g., 'ending December 31, 2034'), use that exact date. Output format: 'Month Day, Year'. Do not include explanatory text. DO NOT include extension option dates or renewal option periods.
Renewal Rights: Extract all information about the tenant's options to renew or extend the lease term. Include: (1) number of renewal options available, (2) duration of each renewal period, (3) conditions for exercising the option, (4) notice requirements, and (5) how renewal rent will be determined.
Early Termination Rights: Extract ALL rights either party has to terminate the lease before the scheduled expiration date. You MUST search the following sections thoroughly: (1) Damage or Destruction/Casualty section - landlord's election not to repair, tenant's right if repairs not completed within specified timeframe; (2) Eminent Domain/Condemnation section - termination rights for total or partial taking that substantially interferes with use; (3) Defaults and Remedies section - termination rights upon default by either party; (4) Assignment/Subletting section - landlord's right to terminate if tenant has material Hazardous Materials issues; (5) Any other sections granting termination rights. For EACH termination right found, include: (a) which party has the right (Tenant or Landlord), (b) the specific conditions triggering the right, (c) notice requirements, (d) any fees or penalties. Present as separate entries for Tenant's Early Termination Rights and Landlord's Early Termination Rights.
Expansion or Contraction Rights: Extract any rights the tenant has to expand into additional space or reduce the leased premises. Include: (1) right of first offer/refusal for adjacent space, (2) contraction options, (3) expansion options, (4) conditions and notice requirements, and (5) how rent adjustments will be calculated.
Relocation Rights: Extract any rights the landlord has to relocate the tenant to different premises within the building or project. Include conditions, notice requirements, landlord obligations for relocation costs, and any tenant remedies.
Security Deposit Amount: Please provide a summary of information from Exhibit A of the document. If the amount of Security Deposit is found, then please only return that amount from the extract.
Security Deposit Form: Extract the form in which the security deposit must be provided (e.g., cash, letter of credit, bond, etc.). Include any specific requirements about the form, such as letter of credit terms, issuing bank requirements, or reduction provisions.
Base Rent: Please find and return the amount(s) for rent if available. It could be Fixed Annual rent, Annual rent, Base Rent, Monthly rent, or Per square foot rate. If available, please include the following details in the abstract (totally skip from response if something is not found): ** Payment schedule (monthly, annually, etc.), ** Any scheduled increases during the initial term. Please clearly highlight the amount(s) found in the response.
Base Rent Abatement: Extract any periods during which base rent is abated (free rent periods). Include: (1) duration of abatement period, (2) when the abatement begins, (3) total dollar value of abatement if stated, (4) conditions under which abatement applies, and (5) what happens if tenant defaults.
Base Rent Increases: Extract information about how and when base rent will increase during the lease term. Include: (1) frequency of increases (annual, every X years, etc.), (2) method of calculation (fixed percentage, CPI adjustment, fixed dollar amount, fair market value, etc.), (3) percentage or amount of increase, and (4) any caps or floors on increases.
Renewal Base Rent: Extract how base rent will be determined for any renewal or extension periods. Include: (1) calculation method (fair market value, percentage increase, fixed rate, etc.), (2) any caps or floors on renewal rent, (3) dispute resolution procedures for rent determination, and (4) comparables or criteria to be used.
Rentable Area: Extract the rentable square footage of the leased premises. Include: (1) total rentable square feet, (2) usable square feet if mentioned, (3) loss factor or add-on factor if stated, and (4) how rentable area is calculated or measured. Present as a specific number with any relevant clarifications.
Tenant's Share: Extract the tenant's proportionate share of building or project expenses (also called Pro Rata Share). This is typically expressed as a percentage. Include: (1) the percentage, (2) how it's calculated (e.g., premises SF / building SF), and (3) whether it's subject to adjustment.
Initial TI Allowance: Extract the tenant improvement allowance provided by landlord for initial build-out. Include: (1) total dollar amount, (2) per square foot amount if stated, (3) what costs it can be applied to, (4) any conditions or deadlines for use, and (5) whether unused amounts are forfeited or credited.
Additional TI Allowance: Extract any additional tenant improvement allowance beyond the initial allowance. Include: (1) amount, (2) conditions for availability, (3) whether it's a loan or grant, (4) repayment terms if applicable.
Management Fee: Extract information about property management fees charged to tenant. Include: (1) calculation method (percentage of base rent, percentage of operating expenses, flat fee, etc.), (2) the specific percentage or amount, (3) whether it's included in operating expenses or billed separately.
Capital Expenditures: Extract provisions regarding capital expenditures and their treatment in operating expenses. IMPORTANT: Distinguish between these SEPARATE line items - do NOT conflate them: (1) 'capital expenditures' as a standalone category, (2) 'costs of repairs and replacements' which is a different category. For capital expenditures specifically, include: (a) whether capital costs can be included in operating expenses, (b) amortization period if allowed, (c) specific types mentioned (e.g., energy savings, code compliance, life safety). Also note if 'Green Capital Expenditures' or environmental/sustainability capital costs are mentioned - if this language is absent from the lease, do NOT assume or infer it exists. Only extract what is explicitly stated.
Operating Expense Exclusions: Extract all items specifically excluded from operating expenses that tenant must reimburse. Common exclusions include: capital improvements, leasing commissions, ground lease payments, debt service, specific repairs, etc. List all exclusions mentioned in the lease.
Assignment/Sublease Rights: Extract the tenant's rights and restrictions regarding assignment of the lease or subleasing the premises. Include: (1) whether assignment/sublease is permitted, (2) landlord consent requirements (e.g., 'not to be unreasonably withheld'), (3) conditions and standards for approval, (4) prohibited transfers, and (5) any exceptions (e.g., transfers to affiliates).
Sublease Recapture Rights: Extract any rights the landlord has to recapture space if tenant proposes to sublease or assign. Include: (1) under what circumstances landlord can recapture, (2) how much space can be recaptured, (3) notice periods, (4) tenant's obligations if landlord recaptures, and (5) whether tenant can withdraw the request.
Tenant's Remedies: Extract tenant's remedies available for landlord's default or breach of lease obligations. Include: (1) types of defaults covered, (2) notice and cure periods, (3) available remedies (e.g., self-help, rent abatement, termination, damages), (4) any limitations on remedies, and (5) conditions for exercising remedies.
Landlord's Remedies: Extract landlord's remedies available for tenant's default or breach. Include: (1) types of defaults, (2) notice and cure periods, (3) available remedies (e.g., termination, damages, re-entry), (4) whether landlord can continue lease and collect rent after default, and (5) tenant's continuing obligations after default.
Insurance Requirements: Extract all insurance requirements for tenant. Include: (1) types of insurance required (general liability, property, etc.), (2) minimum coverage amounts, (3) additional insured requirements, (4) certificate requirements, and (5) any specific policy terms or conditions. List comprehensively.
Maintenance and Repairs: Extract the allocation of maintenance and repair obligations between landlord and tenant. Include: (1) tenant's repair obligations, (2) landlord's repair obligations, (3) structural vs. non-structural responsibilities, (4) HVAC, roof, and other building systems, and (5) any cost-sharing arrangements.
Utilities: Extract provisions regarding utilities. Include: (1) which party pays for which utilities, (2) whether utilities are separately metered or allocated, (3) after-hours HVAC charges if applicable, (4) any caps or limitations on utility charges, and (5) tenant's right to contest charges.
Parking: Extract parking provisions. Include: (1) number of parking spaces allocated to tenant, (2) whether reserved or unreserved, (3) location of spaces, (4) parking charges or fees, (5) ratio of spaces to rentable area, and (6) any additional parking rights or options.
Default Interest Rate: Extract the interest rate charged on late payments or amounts in default. Include: (1) the specific rate (e.g., '5% per annum', 'prime plus 3%'), (2) any maximum rate if capped, and (3) when default interest begins to accrue.
Late Fees: Extract any late fees or charges for late rent payment. Include: (1) the amount or percentage of the late fee, (2) grace period before late fees apply, (3) when late fees are assessed, and (4) whether late fees are in addition to or in lieu of default interest.
Notice Provisions: Extract the notice requirements under the lease. Include: (1) required methods of delivery (certified mail, overnight courier, email, etc.), (2) addresses for notices to each party, (3) when notice is deemed received, and (4) any specific notice requirements for particular lease actions.
Governing Law: Extract which state's laws govern the interpretation and enforcement of the lease. Typically stated as 'This Lease shall be governed by the laws of the State of [State]'.
Dispute Resolution: Extract provisions for resolving disputes between landlord and tenant. Include: (1) whether arbitration or mediation is required, (2) choice of venue for litigation, (3) jury trial waivers if any, (4) prevailing party attorney's fees provisions, and (5) any limitations on damages or remedies.
Alterations: Extract tenant's rights and restrictions regarding alterations or improvements to the premises. Include: (1) what alterations require landlord consent, (2) standard for landlord approval, (3) tenant's obligations regarding permits and compliance, (4) restoration requirements at lease end, and (5) ownership of alterations.
Signage Rights: Extract tenant's rights to signage. Include: (1) interior signage rights, (2) exterior or monument signage rights, (3) building directory listing, (4) size and location restrictions, (5) approval processes, and (6) any signage costs.
Right of First Offer: Extract any right of first offer provisions. Include: (1) what space is subject to ROFO, (2) triggering events, (3) notice and response timeframes, (4) terms on which space must be offered, (5) tenant's acceptance period, and (6) conditions for exercise.
Right of First Refusal: Extract any right of first refusal provisions. Include: (1) what space is subject to ROFR, (2) terms of third-party offer that trigger the right, (3) tenant's matching period, (4) conditions for exercise, and (5) what happens if tenant doesn't exercise.
Purchase Options: Extract any options for tenant to purchase the property or building. Include: (1) purchase price or formula, (2) exercise period and conditions, (3) notice requirements, (4) closing terms, and (5) any credits or offsets.
Subordination: Extract subordination provisions. Include: (1) whether lease is subordinate to mortgages, (2) whether subordination is automatic or requires SNDA, (3) non-disturbance agreement provisions, (4) attornment requirements, and (5) any conditions or limitations on subordination.
Estoppel Certificates: Extract estoppel certificate requirements. Include: (1) timeframe for tenant to respond to estoppel requests, (2) consequences of failure to respond, (3) what information must be certified, (4) number of estoppels required per year, and (5) any limitations on estoppel obligations.
Hazardous Materials: Extract hazardous materials provisions covering both parties. Include: (1) definition of Hazardous Materials, (2) tenant's permitted use of hazardous materials, (3) prohibited materials, (4) disclosure and reporting requirements, (5) compliance obligations for each party, (6) indemnification provisions for each party, (7) cleanup and remediation obligations, (8) landlord's right to maintain environmental insurance. CRITICAL: Only cite section numbers that actually exist in the document - Hazardous Materials is typically in its own numbered section (often Section 39 or similar), NOT Article 21 which is usually Insurance. Verify section numbers before citing.
Casualty: Extract casualty and damage provisions. Include: (1) landlord's repair obligations after casualty, (2) tenant's termination rights, (3) landlord's termination rights, (4) timeframes for repair decisions and completion, (5) rent abatement during repairs, and (6) definition of substantial damage.
Condemnation: Extract condemnation and eminent domain provisions. Include: (1) termination rights for total taking, (2) termination rights for partial taking, (3) rent adjustment for partial taking, (4) award allocation between parties, (5) temporary taking provisions, and (6) what constitutes substantial taking.
Quiet Enjoyment: Extract quiet enjoyment provisions. Include the landlord's covenant that tenant may quietly enjoy the premises without disturbance, and any conditions or limitations on this covenant.
Access Rights: Extract landlord's rights to access the premises. Include: (1) purposes for which landlord may enter, (2) notice requirements, (3) emergency access provisions, (4) tenant's right to accompany landlord, and (5) any limitations on access rights.
Holding Over: Extract holdover provisions. Include: (1) holdover rent rate (typically 125%-200% of base rent), (2) whether holdover creates month-to-month tenancy or tenancy at sufferance, (3) additional charges or penalties, and (4) tenant's obligations to vacate.
Broker Commission: Extract provisions regarding broker commissions. Include: (1) which party pays commission, (2) amount or formula for commission, (3) broker names, (4) indemnification for unauthorized brokers, and (5) when commission is earned and payable.
ADA Compliance: Extract Americans with Disabilities Act compliance obligations. Include: (1) which party is responsible for ADA compliance in premises, (2) building common area compliance responsibility, (3) allocation of costs for required modifications, and (4) any specific ADA-related representations or warranties.
Environmental Compliance: Extract environmental compliance obligations beyond hazardous materials. Include: (1) general environmental law compliance requirements, (2) responsibility for environmental assessments or audits, (3) disclosure obligations, and (4) cost allocation for environmental issues.
Force Majeure: Extract force majeure provisions. Include: (1) definition of force majeure events, (2) which obligations are excused during force majeure, (3) notice requirements, (4) whether rent is abated, (5) termination rights if force majeure continues beyond certain period, and (6) any exceptions.
Confidentiality: Extract confidentiality provisions regarding lease terms. Include: (1) what information must be kept confidential, (2) permitted disclosures, (3) consequences of unauthorized disclosure, and (4) survival of confidentiality obligations.
Liability for Consequential Damage: Extract any provisions limiting or waiving liability for consequential, special, indirect, or punitive damages. Include: (1) whether mutual or one-sided waiver, (2) what types of damages are waived (consequential, special, indirect, punitive, lost profits), (3) any exceptions to the waiver (e.g., specific articles or breaches where waiver does not apply), (4) whether the limitation applies to both landlord and tenant. CRITICAL: Only cite section numbers that actually exist in the document - verify section numbers before citing. Common locations include Limitation of Liability sections, Indemnification sections, or miscellaneous provisions.
Landlord's Hazardous Materials Obligatio: Extract Landlord's specific obligations regarding Hazardous Materials. Include: (1) Landlord's duty to comply with environmental laws for common areas and building systems, (2) Landlord's indemnification obligations for pre-existing contamination or contamination not caused by Tenant, (3) Landlord's disclosure requirements, (4) Landlord's right to maintain environmental insurance as an Operating Expense. Also search the Assignment/Subletting section for Landlord's right to terminate if Tenant or transferee has material Hazardous Materials issues. CRITICAL: Only cite section numbers that actually exist - verify before citing.
Tenant's Hazardous Materials Obligations: Extract Tenant's specific obligations regarding Hazardous Materials. Include: (1) Tenant's permitted use of Hazardous Materials, (2) prohibited materials or activities, (3) compliance with environmental laws, (4) disclosure and reporting requirements, (5) indemnification obligations for contamination caused by Tenant, (6) cleanup and remediation obligations, (7) survival of obligations after lease termination. CRITICAL: Only cite section numbers that actually exist - verify before citing.
Missing Signatures, Exhibits or Informat: Review the lease document for completeness. Identify: (1) any signature blocks that are blank or missing signatures, (2) any exhibits or schedules referenced but not attached or marked as '[Intentionally Omitted]', (3) any blanks or brackets indicating missing information (e.g., '[_______]', 'TBD', 'to be determined'), (4) any conflicting information between different sections of the lease. List all items found.

Abstract Row Focus:
Identify any missing elements, incomplete information, or conflicting data in the lease.

Review For:
1. Missing Signatures: Unsigned signature blocks, missing initials, undated signatures.
2. Missing Exhibits: Referenced exhibits or attachments that are not included (e.g., "See Exhibit B" but Exhibit B is not attached).
3. Blank Fields: Empty spaces where information should be filled in (dates, amounts, names).
4. Incomplete Dates: Partial dates or TBD notations.
5. Conflicting Information: Inconsistent dates, party names, amounts, or terms across different sections.

Output Format:
- If issues are found: List each issue with a brief follow-up action required.
  Example: "• Missing Exhibit B (Floor Plan) - Request from Landlord"
- Limit response to approximately 60 words.

IMPORTANT: Only flag actual issues found in the lease. Do not make assumptions or flag items that are properly completed.
Property Taxes Triggered by Sale: Extract any provisions regarding property tax reassessments or increases triggered by a sale or transfer of the property. Include: (1) whether tenant is responsible for increased taxes due to sale, (2) any caps or limitations on pass-through of sale-triggered tax increases, (3) base year adjustments upon sale.
Holdover Rights: Extract holdover provisions. Include: (1) holdover rent rate (typically 125%-200% of base rent), (2) whether holdover creates month-to-month tenancy or tenancy at sufferance, (3) additional charges or penalties, and (4) tenant's obligations to vacate.
Rights of First Offer/Rights of First Re: Extract tenant's rights of first offer (ROFO) and/or right of first refusal (ROFR) to lease additional space. Include: (1) what space is subject to ROFO/ROFR, (2) triggering events, (3) notice and response timeframes, (4) terms on which space must be offered or matched, (5) tenant's acceptance or matching period.
Rights of First Refusal / Rights of Firs: Extract tenant's right of first refusal or right of first offer to purchase the property or building. Include: (1) triggering events (e.g., landlord's intent to sell), (2) purchase price or formula, (3) notice and exercise periods, (4) closing terms.
Parking Rights: Please provide a formal legal abstract for all the information about the parking provisions (parking lots, parking passes, and parking slots etc.). If available, please include the following details in the abstract (If something from below points is not found, then totally skip it from response): ** Number of parking spaces allocated to tenant ** Whether reserved or unreserved ** Location of spaces ** Parking passes allocated etc. ** Parking charges or fees if any ** Ratio of spaces to rentable area if found ** Any additional parking rights or options. This information can be found in Exhibit A of the lease document too.
Limitation on Landlord's Liability: Extract provisions limiting or capping landlord's liability. Include: (1) types of damages or claims excluded or capped, (2) maximum liability amount if stated, (3) carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, or specific obligations, (4) whether tenant has waived claims against landlord's assets.
Landlord's Utility Obligations: Extract landlord's obligations regarding utilities (e.g., who provides and pays for which utilities, common area utilities, separately metered vs. allocated, after-hours HVAC). Focus on landlord responsibilities. If combined with tenant obligations in one section, extract only landlord-related provisions.
Landlord's Maintenance Obligations: Extract landlord's repair and maintenance obligations. Include: (1) structural repairs, (2) building systems (HVAC, roof, common areas), (3) timeframes for repair, (4) notice requirements. If combined with tenant obligations in one section, extract only landlord-related provisions.
Tenant's Maintenance Obligations: Extract tenant's repair and maintenance obligations. Include: (1) interior repairs, (2) non-structural repairs, (3) HVAC serving premises, (4) compliance with laws. If combined with landlord obligations in one section, extract only tenant-related provisions.
Rent Abatement Rights: Extract tenant's right to abate or reduce rent (separate from base rent abatement/free rent). Include: (1) triggers (e.g., landlord default, casualty, condemnation, failure to provide services), (2) amount or method of abatement, (3) notice and cure, (4) offset or recoupment.
Self-Help Rights: Extract tenant's (or landlord's) right to perform obligations at the other party's expense (self-help, cure, or perform and offset). Include: (1) which party has the right, (2) what obligations can be cured, (3) notice and opportunity to cure, (4) recovery of costs.
Offset Rights: Extract any right to offset or set off amounts (e.g., tenant's right to offset rent against landlord's obligations, or vice versa). Include: (1) which party may offset, (2) what amounts may be offset, (3) notice requirements, (4) limitations.
Loan/Lender Protection Provisions: Extract provisions protecting lenders or addressing mortgage/subordination. Include: (1) lender notice and cure rights, (2) nondisturbance requirements, (3) attornment to lender or purchaser, (4) lease amendments required by lender.
Estoppel: Extract estoppel certificate requirements. Include: (1) timeframe for tenant to respond to estoppel requests, (2) consequences of failure to respond, (3) what information must be certified, (4) number of estoppels required per year, and (5) any limitations on estoppel obligations.
Evidence of Prior Defaults: Extract provisions regarding evidence or disclosure of prior defaults (e.g., tenant's obligation to certify no uncured defaults, or landlord's representation as to tenant's default history).
Casualty Rebuild Period/Condemnation Res: Extract provisions on rebuilding after casualty or restoration after condemnation. Include: (1) timeframes for landlord to repair or rebuild, (2) tenant's rights during rebuild, (3) rent abatement during restoration, (4) what happens if not restored within timeframe.
Casualty/Condemnation Termination Rights: Extract termination rights arising from casualty or condemnation. Include: (1) landlord's right to terminate if not repairing, (2) tenant's right to terminate if substantial damage or taking, (3) notice and timing.
Landlord Notice Address: Extract the address(es) for delivery of notices to the landlord. Include exact address(es) as stated in the lease.
Tenant Notice Address: Extract the address(es) for delivery of notices to the tenant. Include exact address(es) as stated in the lease.
Notices Delivery Methods: Extract required methods for delivering notices (e.g., certified mail, overnight courier, email, hand delivery). Include: (1) permitted methods, (2) when notice is deemed received, (3) any restrictions.
Equity or Other Interests in Tenant Owne: Extract any provisions where landlord holds or may acquire equity or other ownership interests in tenant (or affiliate). Include: (1) type of interest, (2) conditions, (3) consent or disclosure requirements.
Equity or Other Interests in Landlord Ow: Extract any provisions where tenant holds or may acquire equity or other ownership interests in landlord (or affiliate). Include: (1) type of interest, (2) conditions, (3) consent or disclosure requirements.
Other Special Circumstances or Notable P: Extract only the most important material lease terms, special provisions, or notable items not covered by other abstract sections.
Documents Reviewed: List the lease documents reviewed for this abstract (e.g., Lease, First Amendment, Second Amendment, Exhibits A–C). Include document names and dates if stated.
